beats.narration: Tyrannosaurus rex and Stegosaurus get drawn side by side all the time. They never met.
beats.claim: Tyrannosaurus rex and Stegosaurus are separated by a large span of time and did not coexist
beats.visual_question: why would two famous dinosaurs never have crossed paths?
beats.visual_answer: Stegosaurus standing alone on a Jurassic plain, Tyrannosaurus stalking a separate, much later scene, a gap of empty timeline between them

beats.narration: Stegosaurus lived about one hundred fifty-five to one hundred forty-five million years ago, in the late Jurassic.
beats.claim: Stegosaurus lived from about 155 to 145 million years ago
beats.visual_question: when exactly did Stegosaurus walk the Earth?
beats.visual_answer: a timeline band marking one hundred fifty-five to one hundred forty-five million years ago, Stegosaurus standing on it

beats.narration: Tyrannosaurus didn't arrive until the very end of the Cretaceous — around sixty-nine to sixty-six million years ago.
beats.claim: Tyrannosaurus rex lived from about 69 to 66 million years ago
beats.visual_question: how much later did Tyrannosaurus actually show up?
beats.visual_answer: the same timeline band continuing forward, a long gap, then Tyrannosaurus appearing at sixty-nine to sixty-six million years ago

beats.narration: That gap by itself runs at least seventy-six million years — Stegosaurus was already long gone before Tyrannosaurus ever existed.
beats.claim: the gap between the last Stegosaurus and the first Tyrannosaurus rex is roughly 76 to 89 million years
beats.visual_question: how big is the empty stretch of timeline between them?
beats.visual_answer: the timeline band's empty middle section measured out at seventy-six million years, dwarfing both dinosaurs standing at either end

beats.narration: Tyrannosaurus went extinct about sixty-six million years ago. Measured against that same stretch, modern humans sit far closer in time to Tyrannosaurus than Tyrannosaurus ever was to Stegosaurus.
beats.claim: T. rex went extinct about 66 million years ago, and modern humans are far closer to the present than that — closer to T. rex in time than T. rex was to Stegosaurus
beats.visual_question: where do we fit on that same timeline?
beats.visual_answer: the timeline band extending to the present day, a human figure standing near the Tyrannosaurus end, far from the Stegosaurus end

beats.narration: So the next time they're drawn together, remember: Tyrannosaurus is standing closer to us than it ever stood to Stegosaurus.
beats.claim: Tyrannosaurus rex is closer in time to modern humans than it is to Stegosaurus
beats.visual_answer: the full timeline band resolved end to end: Stegosaurus, a vast gap, Tyrannosaurus, a much shorter gap, then the present day
